slides: Your joints aren’t the enemy – your patterns are.
Every day you repeat the same pull‑up depth, squat angle, and foot placement.
Repetitive mis‑alignments force tissue to compensate, breeding pain.
A 5‑minute mobility reset after each session restores true range.
Fix the pattern, and the joints thank you.
Discipline is a chain, not a single lock.
Each tiny decision links to the next, building an unbreakable loop.
When a link fails, the chain weakens, but the rest still holds.
Identify the weakest link—usually the first 10 minutes of your day.
Strengthen that link and the whole chain moves forward.
Energy isn’t stored in carbs; it’s stored in mitochondria.
Mitochondria multiply when you stress them with brief, high‑intensity bouts.
A 30‑second sprint every hour signals them to grow, even on rest days.
Couple that with a nightly protein dose to fuel repair.
More mitochondria = higher baseline energy, no caffeine crash.
Momentum is the silent partner of progress.
It’s created the moment you finish one task and immediately start the next.
The brain treats a seamless handoff as a reward, reinforcing speed.
Schedule a 2‑minute “bridge” between major tasks to keep the flow.
Bridge the gap, and the work carries you forward.
